prompt: A step-by-step cooking coach for pancakes: an ingredient checklist I can tick off, numbered steps with Back and Next buttons, a countdown timer for the current step that I can start and pause, and a progress bar for the whole recipe

A pendulum physics lab: a swinging pendulum, controls to change the string length and the gravity (Earth, Moon and Mars presets), a live readout of the period, and a small chart of the last 10 periods that updates as I change things

A shop for three headphones: browse them on a turntable carousel, pick a color and a size for the selected one, add it to a cart, see a cart panel with quantities I can change, and a checkout summary with subtotal, tax and total

A sprint board with To do, In progress, Review and Done columns, six task cards with priority colors that I can move between columns with arrow buttons, a filter to show only high priority, and a burndown chart that updates when cards reach Done

A smart-home controller with a small 3D model of an apartment: dim the lights per room, a thermostat I can turn up and down, scene buttons (Movie, Dinner, Away) that change several settings at once, and an energy-use chart for today

An interactive model of the bones of the human arm: grab bones to pull them apart and a button to reassemble them, tap a bone to see its name and what it does, and a 5-question quiz with a score and feedback after each answer

A 3-day trip planner for Paris: a 3D map table with six landmark pins, tap a pin for details and buttons to add it to day 1, 2 or 3, an itinerary panel per day with buttons to reorder or remove stops, and the total walking time per day

A mate-in-one chess puzzle on a 3D board: select a piece to highlight its legal moves, move it by pressing a highlighted square, a hint button, an undo button, and a clear success or try-again message

A personal budget dashboard: a donut chart of spending by category, a bar chart of the last six months, tapping a category filters the bar chart to that category, and a savings goal progress ring with a button to log a deposit

A solar system simulator with play and pause, a control for time speed, planet info cards when I tap a planet, toggles for orbit lines and labels, and a 'compare sizes' mode that lines the planets up side by side at true relative size

A 3-step conference registration without a keyboard: choose a ticket type, pick up to two workshops with checkboxes (tell me if I pick too many), choose a t-shirt size with a stepper, then a review screen with Edit buttons for each step and a Confirm button

A mini escape-room puzzle on my desk: a locked box with a 4-digit combination lock I can change digit by digit, three clue objects I can pick up and inspect, a hint button that gives up to three increasingly direct hints, and an opening animation when the code is right
